summary: Python toolkit from Roboflow with reusable computer vision tools for detections, annotations, tracking and datasets.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Supervision is a Python library from Roboflow with reusable tools for computer vision. It takes results from any detection, segmentation or classification model and helps you draw annotations, filter and count detections, track objects and work with datasets.
sixtySeconds.problem: Every computer vision project rewrites the same glue code for drawing boxes, converting formats and counting objects. Supervision provides that code once, and it works with many models.
whoFor: ML engineers working with object detection
Teams processing video for counting or tracking
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a model-agnostic toolkit with ready-made annotators, dataset utilities and connectors for popular models, maintained by Roboflow.

overview: Supervision is model agnostic: you plug in any classification, detection or segmentation model, and connectors convert results into its Detections format. The README example uses RF-DETR, and Roboflow Inference is supported with an API key.
Annotators draw boxes, labels, masks and more onto images and video. Dataset tools load, split, merge and convert datasets between formats.
Install with pip; conda, mamba and source installs are covered in the docs. It is MIT licensed.

firstRun.title: Run a detection
firstRun.code:
import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image
from rfdetr import RFDETRSmall

image = Image.open("path/to/image.jpg")
model = RFDETRSmall()
detections = model.predict(image, threshold=0.5)
len(detections)
